transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
The Russian Defense Ministry says its forces carried out what it calls a massive strike Monday on targets in and around Kiev.
The attack was targeting military industrial complexes, storage sites for cruise missiles and drones, and data centers.
If confirmed, the strikes came one day after Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russian targets.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, is defending President Trump's decision to waive sanctions against Russia.
Speaking to reporters in Uzbekistan this morning, he said the waiver is an effort to bring about peace.
It's because he wants to see if there's an opportunity for the talks that are going on right now with both Ukraine and Russia to lead to something positive and avoid another disastrous year of war and conflict.
French President Emmanuel Macron addressed his country after recent nationwide protests led to scenes of destruction and violence across France.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
Nothing explains it, nothing justifies it, nothing excuses it, he said.
Macron said the majority of protests were peaceful, but small, hardcore, far-left groups joined by "delinquents" came into cities to wreak havoc.
Those who destroyed will pay, those who pillaged will reimburse, and those who wanted to bring down the republic will have to answer for it, he said.
But Macron said those who committed violence should never be confused with protesters with legitimate demands for better learning conditions and worries over rising living costs.
His address is already being criticized by the right for not being tough enough, one law and order politician has called for a state of emergency, and by the left for not proposing real solutions to the young people.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
The AI company Anthropic says it's setting up a public benefit fund for charitable donations, and it's committing 5% of its shares to that fund, as NPR's John Ruich reports. This comes as Anthropic prepares for an initial public offering later this year.
After raising money in May, Anthropic said it was valued at close to a trillion dollars, and some analysts say the IPO could double that.
So the new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will be substantial, and the company says more shares will go into the fund as Anthropic's valuation grows.
As for the kind of donations that the fund could make, Anthropic says an example could be in the labor market, which many experts expect AI to disrupt.
Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing the challenge. The new fund, it says, could enable the company to take bolder action.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Asian shares closed mix in Monday trading as the volatility in technology stocks persists across the world.
South Korea's Kospi closed up 1.1%, while Japan's Nikkei Index lost 0.8%, and China says its economy grew 4.5% for the third quarter.
You're listening to NPR News.
President Trump Sunday endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his re-election campaign.
In a social media post, Trump said Netanyahu has been a great warrior prime minister and an even better partner for peace in fighting Iran.
Do teachers feel like they matter? A new survey finds only one in three teachers say that they do. NPR's Johnaki Mehta has our story.
When educators feel valued, they're less likely to burn out and leave the profession, but a quarter of teachers say they're likely to leave their jobs within a year.
Among those who felt like they matter little or not at all at school, half say they don't plan to stay in education.
All this is from a new survey from Gallup, the Mattering Institute, and the Walton Family Foundation, which is a financial supporter of NPR.
85% of teachers reported their sense of mattering comes through working directly with students and helping them work through difficult situations.
The report says schools and families can take steps to make sure their teachers feel valued by formalizing appreciation, like by making recognition a part of school routines.
Administrators can also have regular conversations around helping school staff grow and develop their careers.
Johnaki Mehta, NPR News.
There was a lot of movement in the AP college football rankings after five of the top seven teams lost Saturday. That's the first time that's ever happened. Miami landed in first, followed by BYU, who jumped six slots after beating Notre Dame.
Ohio State is in third, followed by Notre Dame, Georgia, Indiana, and Ole Miss, Texas Tech, UCLA, and Utah round out the top ten.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

Asian stock markets mixed Monday as technology stock volatility persists; China reports 4.5% growth
Trump endorses Benjamin Netanyahu's re-election campaign in Israel
